diagnostic_evidence.quote: where such an approximate design curve is a curve satisfying a condition equivalent to Definition \ref{def:design} but where the $L^p$ norm $||\cdot||_p$ is used instead of the $L^\infty$ (supremum) norm.

issues.failure_explanation: The quantity |sup f| is not the L-infinity norm. For f=-x_1^2, sup f=0 while ||f||_infty=1, so the condition would force exact equality for such f. This makes the definition mathematically ill-posed as an approximate design condition.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace |sup f| with sup |f| (equivalently ||f||_infty) throughout the definition and subsequent uses.
issues.overall_effect: All approximate t-design curve results are stated with a non-norm error bound, so their guarantees are not the intended L-infinity approximate design statements.
issues.title: Approximate design definition uses |sup f| instead of sup |f|
issues.why_classification: The correction is local and forced; it preserves all substantive claims and only fixes the error norm.

issues.failure_explanation: Without dividing by \lambda(x_i), the endpoint of interval i is (-1)^i(2\lambda(x_i)-1), while the next interval starts at (-1)^i. Continuity requires \lambda(x_i)=1 for every i, impossible for a weighted design set with more than one point. The proof's substitution ds=\lambda(x_i)/2\,du is therefore invalid.

failure_location.quote: w_\Bbb R(s)=(-1)^i(2(s-\Lambda_{i-1})-1), \quad w_{\Bbb R^d}(s)=\sqrt{1-w_\Bbb R(s)^2}M(w_\Bbb R(s))x_i

issues.overall_effect: The general construction of weighted t-design curves from weighted t-design sets is ill-defined; Theorems weight and weightstrength relying on it are unproven as stated.
issues.title: Weighted curve construction omits division by weight in w_R
issues.why_classification: The repair is a short local correction, but the construction is central and the proof depends on the missing factor; without it the curve is not even continuous.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: whose preimages $h^{-1}(s)$ we equip with the standard spherical measure $\sigma$ normalized so that $\sigma(h^{-1}(s))=1$

issues.failure_explanation: For d\neq2, the normalized spherical measure on S^d does not decompose as (1/2)\,ds\times\sigma_{slice}. The correct density in the first coordinate is proportional to (1-s^2)^{(d-2)/2}. For f(\omega)=\omega_1^2, the construction gives average 1/3, while the true average on S^d is 1/(d+1); for d=3 this is 1/3\neq1/4. Hence w_{X,M} is not a weighted t-design curve for d\geq3.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Modify the construction so that the first coordinate is distributed with density (1-u^2)^{(d-2)/2}\,du, or add a compensating weight depending on u; this requires changing the construction and proof.
issues.overall_effect: The general construction fails to produce weighted t-design curves on S^d for d\geq3, so the main existence theorem for d\geq4 and the fixed-strength theorem are unproven.
issues.title: Weighted curve proof uses incorrect slice measure decomposition
issues.why_classification: The advertised regime d\geq3 is not covered by the construction; repairing it requires a new argument or construction, not just a local fix.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We then take $W_Y$ to be double the sum of all weights of edges of $\mathcal T_Y$

issues.failure_explanation: The inequality W_t\leq(|Y_t|-1)\rho_t/4 is false for the covering radius \rho_t. Even with the minimal separation D_t from Proposition \ref{pro:covrad}, the MST total weight is not bounded by N D_t/4; for two points W=2d and D=d/2, so W=4D. Moreover, Proposition \ref{pro:covrad} bounds the packing radius D_t, not the covering radius \rho_t. Thus the derivation W_t\lesssim t^{2n-1} is unsupported.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the false bound with a correct upper bound W_t\leq C|Y_t|\rho_t and cite or prove that the covering radius of the design sets is \asymp 1/t.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of the asymptotic length bound in Theorem main is invalid; the main approximate t-design cycle result is not established by the given argument.
issues.title: Proof of main approximate theorem uses false W_t bound and wrong radius
issues.why_classification: The asymptotic conclusion may still hold with a correct constant and covering radius bound, but the proof requires a nontrivial correction.

issues.failure_explanation: The equality assumes \int_{\gamma|_l} f equals the arc-length integral of f over L\cap\gamma([0,1]) without multiplicity. If \gamma traverses L multiple times, the integral over \gamma|_l counts multiplicity while \int_L f\,ds does not. Counterexample: d=1, L=S^1, \gamma(s)=e^{4\pi i s}, f=1, c=1/(2\pi). Then \varepsilon_\gamma=-1 and the claimed inequality fails.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add hypotheses that \gamma is simple and that on l it parametrizes L\cap\gamma([0,1]) exactly once with arc-length measure, or revise the error term to account for multiplicity.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of Theorem const and the smoothing lemma rely on a false comparison lemma; the approximate design guarantees for the constructed cycles are not established by this lemma as stated.
issues.title: Overlap lemma ignores multiplicity of curve on L
issues.why_classification: The lemma is false in general, but the main application uses simple \gamma, so a localized repair may suffice; however it affects several results.
